name: Claim
sourceRefs: apiv/dzero lib/dzero/segments/07_claim.rb (field-id-to-symbol dictionary, read directly) cross-confirmed against eduardonunesp/ncpdp-telecom-fmt-book docs/segments.md's own worked Claim Segment (AM07) example.

Deliberately NOT modeled this pass (core fields, not exhaustive, matching this codebase's own EDI 835/837 precedent): SE/ER (procedure modifier), EW/EX (intermediary authorization), HD/HF/HG (dispensing status), NV (delay reason code), N4 (Medicaid ICN), U7 (pharmacy service type), MT (patient assignment indicator) -- all present in dzero's own dictionary but genuinely niche for a first-phase B1 claim.

quantityDispensed modeled with places=3 (NOT the places=2 an initial draft took directly from data-types.md's own PROSE claim of 'implied 2 decimal places') -- a real, deliberate correction found by checking the doc's own WORKED EXAMPLE arithmetic rather than trusting its prose: the raw value '0000030000' (10 digits, =30000 as a plain integer) does NOT reconcile with 2 places (30000/100=300.00, contradicting the doc's own stated '30.00' result) but DOES reconcile cleanly with 3 places (30000/1000=30.000, matching '30.00' modulo one insignificant trailing zero the prose likely rounded off when writing it up). 3 implied decimal places is also the long-established real-world NCPDP convention for quantity fields generally. width=10 is directly, byte-for-byte confirmed from the same example regardless of which precision is right. quantityPrescribed/originallyPrescribedQuantity reuse the same places=3 convention but have no independently confirmed width of their own -- left unset.
fillNumber (D3) width=2 and daysSupply (D5) width=3 are directly, byte-for-byte confirmed from the same worked Claim Segment example ('D301'->01, 'D5030'->030).

productServiceIdQualifier(E1)/productServiceId(D7)/quantityDispensed(E7)/fillNumber(D3)/daysSupply(D5)/datePrescriptionWritten(DE) widened from required=true to required=false (2026-09-20) to support B2 (Claim Reversal) reusing this SAME shared segment -- confirmed directly from a real, official payer sheet (State of North Dakota Medicaid NCPDP D.0 payer sheet, 'B1-B2-B3-E1 Payer Sheet Exclusion.pdf', section 2 'Claim Reversal Transaction'): B2's own Claim Segment table lists ONLY 455-EM (Prescription/Service Reference Number Qualifier) and 402-D2 (Prescription/Service Reference Number) as Mandatory -- every other Claim field is excluded from B2's own template entirely (the payer sheet's own legend: fields excluded from a transaction's template are Not Used for it). A PURELY PERMISSIVE widening matching this codebase's own established EDI X12 precedent (e.g. CLAUDE.md's 'CL1/SV1/SV2/TRN/UM usage widened globally, purely permissive, zero behavior change for every existing consumer') -- every real B1 fixture already supplies these fields in practice (a complete B1 claim naturally has them), so B1's own validation behavior is unaffected; only B2's genuinely narrower real-world claim segment now validates correctly.
